messages:
maria_support: FYI escalation from Acme — they say their monthly credits dropped to 0 ~20m before expected reset and UI stayed at 0 after midnight. Ticket #SUP-1298.
ryan_infra: Can you drop the tenant id and any logs? quick check I can run.
maria_support: Tenant 88f4c2. Customer says they run a long ingest job over websockets; they see continuous token burn. They attached a small log snippet and a screengrab of the billing page showing 00:00 refill scheduled but balance stayed 0 for ~20m.
ryan_infra: Pulling logs now... I see a reconnect storm pattern: the client is opening a new stream every ~5s with the same connection label. Each connect emits a session_start event and we charge initial system+prompt tokens per new session because the client isn't sending an idempotency key.
maria_support: Is that the same as the streaming double-charge we fixed earlier?
ryan_infra: Related but different. Previously we double-counted within a single stream when chunking failed. Here the client repeatedly opens brand-new sessions; server treats each as a fresh invocation and bills the initial context each time. Also, and this is important for the refill behavior, our monthly-reset job currently defers refill for tenants with "active persistent sessions" to avoid immediate negative balance churn — the system thought the tenant was still 'active' because sessions kept restarting, so the UI showed 0 until the background guard cleared.
emma_billing: So both the rapid charges and the guard explain the delay. Can we fix the customer immediately?
ryan_infra: Short term: we can do a one-off credit patch to bring them back above their monthly threshold. Mid-term: require clients to send an idempotency header on stream connect (X-Redwood-Idempotency) so reconnects are deduped for billing, and tweak the reset job so it doesn't hold refill indefinitely when reconnect rates are obviously retry storms.
ryan_infra: Logs (sanitized):
```
[2024-06-20T23:59:50Z] tenant=88f4c2 session_start conn=ingest-conn id=null tokens_charged=1200
[2024-06-20T23:59:55Z] tenant=88f4c2 session_start conn=ingest-conn id=null tokens_charged=1100
[2024-06-20T23:59:59Z] tenant=88f4c2 session_start conn=ingest-conn id=null tokens_charged=1150
... repeated every 4-6s ...
```
ryan_infra: Repro steps for support/SE to give customer: 1) Confirm their client isn't doing an auto-reconnect loop. 2) If they must reconnect, add header `X-Redwood-Idempotency: <session-uuid>` on connect so we treat reconnects as same billing session. 3) As immediate mitigation they can reduce reconnect frequency or add exponential backoff.
maria_support: I'll pass these steps to the customer now and offer the temporary credit patch.
emma_billing: Please log the credit patch amount and get explicit customer approval before applying. Finance needs a note for reconciliation.
ryan_infra: I've queued a one-time +500k token patch for tenant 88f4c2 pending approval from the customer; also opened a follow-up infra ticket to relax the reset-block logic and add a metric to detect reconnect storms.
maria_support: Customer confirmed they can add the idempotency header and will roll a fix within their next deploy (ETA 3h). Tokens stopped spiking in our staging repro once they added the idempotency header. They asked us to apply the patch immediately.
emma_billing: Patch approved on record; I'll update the billing ticket.
maria_support: Closing the escalation after patch applied and customer confirmed stabilization. Thanks team :tada:
replay-bot: Ticket SUP-1298 updated by maria_support — status: resolved (one-off credit applied, customer deployed idempotency fix.)
